hook_text: One sheet tells the builder what to make. One chart tells you how, in order, with checks. Both before you cut a thing.
clip_script: Turn the Final Idea into a working drawing: plan under elevation, end view opposite, a section through the ramp showing slab, fill and kerb. 1:50, every size once, title block. For a turning ramp, the plan tells most. Then check it against the brief, spec by spec: leg length over rise is 12 or more, risers 4 at 150, landings 1 200, rails at 900. Fix any fail on the paper, not in your head. Now the flow chart: oval start, boxes for jobs, diamonds for checks. Convert to 1:20, mark the base, cut the legs, check the gradient, glue, cut the steps, check the risers, posts, rails, paint, final check, end. Checks after cutting, before gluing, where mistakes are cheap.
visual_style: Whiteboard A3 sheet with plan, elevation and section appearing; a tick list beside it; then a flow chart drawing itself downward with two diamonds and loop-back arrows.
mood: Organised, anticipatory, calm before the build.
pacing: Drawing in fifteen seconds, the check, the chart with its diamonds.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and flow-chart making a cup of tea with one decision diamond.
